about: The fixed list of measures per lens (DRAFT, for a planner to approve). Drawn from the pilot's 410 keys and the Planner Research Taxonomy's standing questions. key = <lens prefix>.<measure>. cardinality: one = a single value per period (and per qualifier) whose rivals contest; many = a list whose items sit side by side and never contest. qualifier: what distinguishes one row of the measure from another (none, player, channel, segment, moment, statement, rule, body, parent, metric, campaign). group: which targeted search finds it (1-3 per lens).

groups.1: market size and growth: value, volume, growth rates, consumption per head
groups.2: players and shares: the leading players, their market shares, the top brands, how many players
groups.3: structure: channel split (on-trade, off-trade, online), segments, exports, consolidation and deals

measures.definition: Total market value in the period.
Total market volume in the period, in the unit stated (litres, cases, units).
Year-on-year change in market value.
Year-on-year change in market volume.
Consumption per head (or per adult) in the period, in the unit stated.
The category's share of a wider market BY VALUE (sales value), e.g. of the 'alcohol market'.
The category's share of a wider market BY VOLUME (litres, units, cases), e.g. of the 'alcohol market'.
The market-leading player or brand. The value is its name only (e.g. 'Bulmers'), nothing else.
A named player's or brand's share of the market.
Combined share of the top N players (qualifier: e.g. 'top 5').
Number of players, brands or producers in the market.
Share of sales through a channel (qualifier: on-trade, off-trade, online, forecourt...).
Share of the market held by a product segment (qualifier: the segment).
Value of exports in the period.
A merger, acquisition, entry or exit in the market.

groups.1: brand claims and assets: what each brand says it stands for, its lines and distinctive assets, its price position
groups.2: brand moves: launches, campaigns, sponsorships, agency appointments
groups.3: brand measures: prompted awareness, number of brands

measures.definition: A claim or line a brand uses about itself.
A distinctive brand asset (character, sound, visual, pack).
Where the brand sits on price (value, mainstream, premium).
A product or range launch.
A named campaign and what it said.
A sponsorship or partnership.
An agency appointed or changed, and for what.
Prompted awareness of a brand.
Number of brands competing in the category.

groups.1: who buys: penetration, segments, purchase frequency and occasions
groups.2: attitudes: survey findings on attitudes, barriers and motivations, with the share who hold them
groups.3: culture: live cultural tensions and trends around the category

measures.definition: Share of households or adults who buy (qualifier: the population, e.g. 'all adults', '18-34').
A buyer segment's share of buyers or spend.
An occasion the category is bought or used for.
Share of people agreeing with a stated attitude (qualifier: the statement, short).
An attitude or belief about the category, without a figure.
A reason people do not buy or buy less.
A reason people buy.
A live cultural tension the category sits in.
A consumer trend affecting the category.

groups.1: advertising conventions: what every ad in the category does, its visual, verbal and sound codes
groups.2: worn-out and challenger codes: the cliches, and brands that break the conventions

measures.definition: A convention most ads in the category follow.
A recurring visual convention.
A recurring verbal or claim convention.
A recurring music or sound convention.
A convention described as tired or cliched.
A brand breaking the category's conventions, and how.

groups.1: the calendar: seasonal peaks, key moments, launch windows and cycles
groups.2: moments in figures: share of sales in peak periods, spend and sales growth around moments

measures.definition: A moment the category plans around (a season, event, holiday).
When launches usually happen.
A buying or contract cycle (renewals, contract ends, weather).
Share of annual sales in a period (qualifier: the period, e.g. 'Q4', 'Christmas').
Consumer spend at a moment (qualifier: the moment).
Change in sales around a moment against the year before.

groups.1: total and category advertising spend, and its growth
groups.2: spend by channel: TV, radio, outdoor, digital, social, search, display; channel shares
groups.3: share of voice and the cost of attention (CPM, cost per reach)

measures.definition: Total advertising spend (qualifier: 'whole market' or the category).
Year-on-year change in advertising spend (qualifier as above).
Forecast advertising spend for a coming period.
Spend in one channel (qualifier: tv, radio, outdoor, digital, social, search, display, print, cinema).
A channel's share of spend.
A brand's share of category advertising.
Cost per thousand or per reach point in a channel.

groups.1: which codes and laws apply, which regulator enforces them, and what needs pre-clearance
groups.2: what you cannot say: restrictions, mandatory copy, substantiation, age and audience rules
groups.3: what is changing: pending legislation, recent rulings and enforcement, grants and levies

measures.definition: A code or law that applies to the category's marketing (qualifier: the body).
Whether ads need pre-clearance (qualifier: the clearing body).
Something marketing may not do (timing, audience, placement, content).
Wording or warnings that must appear.
What claims must be backed by, and how.
An age limit in the rules (qualifier: the rule, e.g. 'people shown in ads').
A proposed or scheduled change to the rules, with its date if known.
A recent ruling or enforcement action and its outcome.
A levy, deposit or fee set by the rules (qualifier: what it applies to).
A grant or incentive available in the category.

groups.1: award-winning and published effectiveness cases in the category and what they achieved
groups.2: evidence on what works: long vs short term, share of voice, pricing power

measures.definition: A published effectiveness case: the brand, campaign and what it did.
A measured result of a named campaign (qualifier: the campaign).
An effectiveness or creative award won in the category.
A finding on what works in the category (long vs short, share of voice, pricing).
